title: Every player gets the same cards
concept: Aliased mutable objects from list multiplication
symptom: Dealing 2 cards each to 2 players prints [[9, 8, 7, 6], [9, 8, 7, 6]]. The deck does shrink by 4 as expected.
rootCause: [[]] * n makes n references to one list. Every append goes to the same hand, so all players print the same 4 cards while the deck shrinks correctly.

wrongFixes.whyWrong: Copying the deck makes the hands right, but deal no longer removes dealt cards from the caller's deck, which other code relies on.

grading.question: Why does the deck shrink correctly while the hands are wrong?
grading.ideal: pop() acts on deck; only the hands are aliased.

grading.question: Name the Python idiom that creates n independent empty lists.

turns.text: Dealing 2 cards to 2 players gives both players the same four cards.
[[]] * n_players makes every hand the same list. I build the hands with a comprehension, and while I was there I made deal work on a copy of the deck so it no longer changes the caller's list.
Fixed: each player now gets two different cards.

transcript.verdict: The comprehension is the fix; the extra change is a new bug. deal() is meant to remove dealt cards from the caller's deck, and other code relies on the deck shrinking. Copying it 'while I was there' changed behaviour nobody asked about. Ask for the one-line fix alone.
